scope_note: Named self-declared ethnicity, people or group categories in Brazil’s 2022 census. These are census categories, not a count of governments, legal recognition decisions or a complete inventory of Indigenous identities. Countries indicates the census scope, not an exclusive homeland.
extraction_note: Table 20 has 404 data rows. Twelve subtotal headings and the residual response Outra etnia das Américas are excluded, leaving 391 distinct named leaf categories. All 404 table labels and their subtotal/leaf roles reconcile with the current IBGE dashboard’s numbered indicator list. Seven repeated labels are subtotal/child pairs, not duplicate peoples. The eight named leaf categories under Outras etnias das Américas remain included. Source spellings are preserved; name removes only a trailing footnote marker while directory_name preserves the exact table label.
edition_note: This table reports 2022 census data and was served with an October 23, 2025 modification date. A revised 2026 edition of this table was not established in this source review.

review.method: Two independent local parsers and dashboard/table reconciliation; no identity crosswalk approval.

source_identifier_note: ibge_indicator_id is the dashboard’s official statistical indicator identifier, not a legal, government or ethnicity classification code. The directory prefix is local.

excluded_residual_responses.label: Outra etnia das Américas
excluded_residual_responses.reason: Unspecified residual response, not a named leaf category.

dashboard_exclusion_note: The dashboard’s note excludes nonidentifying responses and the Outras etnias das Américas aggregate. This extraction excludes the aggregate row, while retaining its eight specifically named children, which reconciles the stated 391 count.

source_footnotes.*: IBGE flags these self-declared labels in relation to historical classifications of disappearance. This is a source annotation, not a present-day extinction finding.
source_footnotes.**: IBGE reports this linguistic-family label as respondents declared it for ethnicity.

multiple_declarations_note: The census permitted up to two ethnicity declarations per Indigenous person. No person counts or percentages are exported here.

public_notes: Source footnote markers are annotations, not part of the displayed names. The single-asterisk note concerns names historically classified as having disappeared that people self-declared in this census. It is not a claim that these peoples are extinct.

The double-asterisk note flags responses understood as linguistic families and published as declared. These source categories are not silently converted into separate governments or definitive people-level identities.
public_extraction_note: This list keeps the named census categories. Subtotal headings and an unnamed other-Americas response are excluded; named responses from other parts of the Americas remain visible. Source spellings are preserved, with footnote markers shown separately.
